Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent No.3.
ORDER The present appeals have been filed by the appellants against the award dated 3.8.2016 passed by the claims Tribunal in Claim Case No.450/2013.

The Insurance Company has preferred M.A.No.1844/2016 on the ground that this was a case of false implication of the vehicle and M.A.No.1989/2016 has been filed on the ground that compensation awarded is not just and proper.

2. The facts of the case are that on 17.4.2012 at around 7.30 PM deceased Raju and Jagdish were walking towards Susari on Khandwa-Baroda Highway Road, when they reached near Kukshi College, respondent No.1 came driving the vehicle MP-46-G-0916 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into both the persons.
Both of them sustained injuries and Raju died during treatment.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17599 2 MA-1844-2016 2.1
Appellant/claimant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
The claims Tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.38,375/- to the appellant/claimant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the present is a case of false implication of the vehicle.
He submits that the FIR was registered on 24.4.2012 for an incident, which happened on 17.4.2012, thus he submits that the FIR was delayed by seven days.
he also submits that it is a clear case of false implication of vehicle because it has come in the evidence that the concerned vehicle was seen at some other place.
He states that on 17.4.2012 the vehicle was at Toll Tax Barrier at 8.27 PM.
Thus, he states that in fact the vehicle was not there at the time of incident at 7.30 PM at the spot of accident.
He emphasised that delay of seven days clearly indicates that the vehicle was falsely implicated so as to get the compensation.
4. In response to the submissions made by the counsel for the appellant, counsel for the respondent/claimant submitted that it is not a case of delayed FIR.
He submits that in fact the report of Marg was given on 18.4.2012 at 7.40 morning itself.
By referring to para 9 of the impugned award he submits that it was duly considered by the claims Tribunal.
It is in fact a case where the Police had investigated the matter and registered FIR on a subsequent date i.e. 24.4.2012.
Thus, the intimation was given immediately because the accident had occurred at around 7.30 PM on 17.4.2012 and the same was reported in the morning of 18.4.2012.
Learned counsel for the claimant submits that the claimant has suffered 30% disability.

5. Interestingly, this Court has carefully considered entire evidence, but it NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17599 3 MA-1844-2016 has not come anywhere in the entire evidence that the vehicle in question could not have been present at both the places, which becomes very significant in view of the fact that the time of presence of vehicle is different at those places.
Thus, in view of the above facts the appeal of the Insurance Company has no substance.
6. From the discussion made in para 15 to 18 of the award it is seen that the Tribunal has not found any permanent disability in the case of claimant.

This Court has also considered the evidence, which is on record including Ex.A/15, which a certificate issued by the private practitioner and not in the capacity of Orthopedic of the Government Hospital.
The findings of the claims Tribunal in view of the evidence as seen by this Court also appears to be impeccable.
The claims Tribunal has already awarded an amount of Rs.38,375/- to the appellant, thus facts of the present case does not appear to be interfered with on the ground of quantum of compensation.
7. Resultantly, both the appeals fail and are hereby dismissed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil Icici Lombard General Insurance Co Ltd. vs Jagdish @ Posaram on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22315042/
